purpose: Phase-8A acquired (persistent) resistance model. Acquired resistance is a PERSISTENT reduction in treatment sensitivity that emerges AFTER exposure and requires stronger, temporal evidence than transient adaptation. It must NOT be classified after a single unsupported frame, and it must NEVER be inferred from a delivery-limited response. Each state defines a bounded sensitivity-reduction modifier, persistence linkage, and evidence. No invented mutation / gene / IC50 shift / time-to-resistance / fold-resistance (all NOT_REPORTED).

coefficient_policy.0_interpretation: 0 = no acquired reduction in treatment sensitivity
coefficient_policy.1_interpretation: 1 = maximal schematic acquired reduction the model represents
coefficient_policy.source: general acquired-resistance biology applied predictively; NO experimental acquired-resistance dataset exists for this context in the frozen package
coefficient_policy.sensitivity_note: acquired reduction persists across washout per persistence criteria; applied only through a bounded adapter.
coefficient_policy.limitations: No mutation identity/frequency, IC50 shift, fold-resistance, or time-to-resistance is stated (all NOT_REPORTED).

suspected.meaning: Persistence signal suspected; not yet supported.

emerging.meaning: Acquired resistance emerging with supporting temporal signal.

established.meaning: Acquired resistance established across multiple exposure stages.

partially_reversible.meaning: Acquired resistance partially reversing where supported.

rules.requires_temporal_evidence: Acquired resistance requires temporal evidence (multiple stages / washout persistence / rechallenge reduction) OR an explicitly labelled prediction; never a single unsupported frame.
rules.not_delivery_failure: A delivery-limited or uptake-limited response is never promoted to acquired resistance.
rules.minimum_exposure_stages_note: SUSPECTED -> EMERGING requires at least this many supported exposure stages (schematic threshold; see persistent-resistance registry).
